Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: DPA & Order Form — Aurelia Health: legal redlines and KMS options

Hi Olga / Marissa,

Thanks for the fast turnaround on the MSA draft. Attached is Aurelia's redline of the DPA and a short summary of our asks (Aurelia_DPA_Redline.docx, DPA_Summary_v1.pdf). We're working toward a procurement sign-off target next week and need to lock the privacy/transfer language this week if possible.

Key asks from our side:
- We need to confirm support for customer-managed keys (customer KMS) when Redwood is deployed in our VPC/private deployment. Our security team requires KMS ownership + key rotation controls.
- Can you confirm that the SCCs text you provided maps to the latest EU Commission SCCs and whether you are amenable to a short transfer addendum we proposed (see redline, section 4)?
- We also requested a current subprocessor list snapshot and an audit log sample (export control evidence) for SOC2 / GDPR internal review — can you provide an ETA?

If these items are a blocker for signing the order form, flag them now. Happy to hop on a short call — Anna Ruiz (copied) will lead procurement.

Attachments: Aurelia_DPA_Redline.docx (redline), DPA_Summary_v1.pdf (one-pager)

Thanks,
Peter Smyth

Peter — thanks for sending the redline and the clear summary. We received the attachments and I'll coordinate internal triage. Quick timeline and next steps from Redwood: 

1) Legal triage: I'll lead the DPA review and aim to get a consolidated response by EOD Tue (2028-05-15).
2) Product/Infra check: Karhtik to confirm feasibility and any service-impact notes for customer-managed KMS and VPC private deployments.
3) Evidence & audit artifacts: Marissa will pull the current subprocessor list and a redacted audit log sample for your review; ETA is 48 hours.

Questions for you (so we can scope the call):
- Is your preferred deployment model 'VPC + customer KMS' (cloud-hosted) or true on-prem private deployment? The redline references both, and the technical constraints differ.
- For the transfer addendum: are you asking for expanded SCCs mapping OR a separate one-page addendum that calls out EU Commission SCCs with an annex?

I'll wait on Karhtik and Marissa and then consolidate a single reply + proposed redline. Would you prefer a 30-min call Tue morning or Tue afternoon?

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example
To: olga_petrov@redwood.example, marissa_cole@redwood.example
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: tech check — Aurelia KMS / VPC / order form implications

Folks — quick infra readout so legal can shape responses:

Summary:
- VPC private deployment + customer-managed KMS (cloud KMS customer controls) is supported on our Private offering. We integrate with customer KMS via envelope encryption; customer retains key control.
- On-prem agent (air-gapped) has more constraints: HSM-certified key material must be provided or we need an approved agent install; that path is longer (2-4 weeks ops work).

Implications for contract language:
- We can accept customer KMS language if we add a short operational clause: customer acknowledges that certain debug/diagnostic logs may require temporary keys accessible to Redwood for incident response, limited to defined types and with strong audit controls.
- Proposed bilingual redline snippet (proposed-dpa-snippet.txt attached):

"If Customer elects customer-managed encryption keys for Private deployment, Redwood will integrate using envelope encryption. Customer is responsible for KMS configuration and rotation. Redwood will not export or persist customer key material. In exceptional incident response scenarios, Redwood may request temporary limited access as mutually agreed in writing; such access will be scoped, time-limited, and logged."

Price/Order Form note: enabling customer-managed KMS on Private may require a small ops surcharge in the order form (we run a manual onboarding & verification). I recommend we surface a one-time onboarding fee in the order form Annex A.

I'll attach a plain-text snippet (proposed-dpa-snippet.txt) and a short ops checklist. If legal wants firmer language on incident access, I can iterate.

Karthik
Head of Infrastructure Integrations (technical lead)
Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov@redwood.example
To: Peter Smyth <peter.smyth@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 15 May 2028 23:40:00 +0000
Subject: RE: DPA & Order Form — Aurelia Health: legal redlines and KMS options

Peter / Anna — thanks again for the redline. Quick consolidated update and proposal: 

1) Customer-managed KMS: Redwood can support customer-managed keys for Private (VPC) deployments. We accept the DPA language with the operational guardrail proposed by Karthik. I've attached a revised DPA page that incorporates the proposed snippet and limited incident-access guardrail (attachment: Aurelia_DPA_Redline_v2.docx).

2) SCCs & transfer addendum: We confirm we map to the latest EU Commission SCCs. Rather than expanding the MSA, we suggest a separate one-page Transfer Addendum that references the Commission SCC set and includes the subprocessor list snapshot as Annex 1 — this keeps the order form cleaner.

3) Evidence & artifacts: Marissa will send the subprocessor list and a redacted audit log sample within 48 hours (CC'd). Expect two attachments shortly.

4) Order form pricing: As Karthik noted, customer-managed KMS on Private requires an onboarding verification. Proposed one-time onboarding fee: 
- Onboarding & KMS verification: $6,000 (one-time).

Action items:
- If Aurelia is comfortable with the attached DPA v2 and the Transfer Addendum approach, we will:
  a) upload the Order Form + DPA v2 to DocuSign and share a link;
  b) Marissa will attach the subprocessor list and audit sample;
  c) Karhtik will prepare a short ops-runbook for the onboarding.

Proposed call: Wed 17 May, 30 minutes — 09:00 BST or 15:00 BST? Please confirm which works for you.
